newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-SICK TOMBA DECIDES TO MISS WENGEN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SICK TOMBA DECIDES TO MISS WENGEN.

text.p: Alberto Tomba will not race in Sunday's Alpine skiing World Cup slalom in Wengen.

The Italian ski federation said in a statement on Friday that Tomba, after training in Madonna di Campiglio, had still not fully recovered from the influenza that forced him to withdraw from a slalom in Chamonix, France, last weekend.
It said his doctor Herbert Schoenhuber had advised him not to take part in the race in Switzerland.
"He has returned home and will rest for two or three days before re-starting training in preparation for Kitzbuehel," the federation said in a statement.
In Chamonix, the triple Olympic champion was second fastest in the first leg of a slalom before pulling out.
The world slalom and giant slalom champion also missed a giant in Adelboden, Switzerland, this week.

His absence there sent him tumbling out of the World Cup giant slalom top 15 rankings for the first time in 10 years -- something he does not risk in slalom having finished second at Madonna di Campiglio just before Christmas.
Tomba, who crashed heavily in pre-season training and injured a wrist and knee, has struggled to get back to his old form and has completed only two races this season.
The skier has said his main concern is to get fit in time for the world championships in Sestriere, which start at the beginning of February.
